articles.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an exoplanet that "disappeared" after seven years of observations.
articles.body: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world.

articles.title: Why create-next-app Isn't Enough: Scaffolding by Product Type, Not Stack
articles.excerpt: In the last article, I said I keep rebuilding the same app. Before writing any code, I wanted to answer a fair question: don't tools for this already exist? They do, and they're good. So here's what I…
articles.body: In the last article, I said I keep rebuilding the same app. Before writing any code, I wanted to answer a fair question: don't tools for this already exist? They do, and they're good. So here's what I found. Two families of tools Starting a project today usually means picking from one of two families. Family 1: Scaffolders. You run a command, answer questions about your tech, and get a project. create-next-app is the plainest version: it's Vercel's official scaffold, and it has no opinions about auth, payments, databases, or similar concerns. create-t3-app goes further. It's a modular CLI that generates full-stack, type-safe Next.js apps, and the stack covers tRPC, Tailwind, Prisma or Drizzle, and NextAuth. Each technology can be selected independently of the others.

articles.title: Guardrail para advocacia
articles.excerpt: Resposta curta Guardrails para advocacia são mecanismos técnicos e éticos que restringem o uso de IA em atividades jurídicas sensíveis — como redação de petições, análise de provas ou orientação proce…
articles.body: Resposta curta Guardrails para advocacia são mecanismos técnicos e éticos que restringem o uso de IA em atividades jurídicas sensíveis — como redação de petições, análise de provas ou orientação processual — garantindo conformidade com o Estatuto da OAB e a Resolução 05/2023 do Conselho Federal da OAB. Eles impedem a autonomia plena da IA na prática da advocacia, exigindo supervisão humana contínua. TL;DR A OAB proíbe a atribuição de responsabilidade profissional a sistemas de IA (Resolução CF/OAB nº 05/2023, art. 2º). Advogados devem manter controle integral sobre conteúdos gerados por IA — inclusive revisão crítica e assunção de responsabilidade (art. 3º).
articles.author: Matheus Feijão

articles.title: Guardrail para Claude, GPT e próprio
articles.excerpt: Resposta curta Guardrails para Claude, GPT e modelos próprios são camadas técnicas e políticas que limitam saídas inseguras, não éticas ou ilegais — aplicadas via filtragem de entrada/saída, classific…
articles.body: Resposta curta Guardrails para Claude, GPT e modelos próprios são camadas técnicas e políticas que limitam saídas inseguras, não éticas ou ilegais — aplicadas via filtragem de entrada/saída, classificação de conteúdo, regras de negação e RLHF. Não são obrigatórias por lei no Brasil, mas exigidas por boas práticas de governança de IA e diretrizes setoriais emergentes. TL;DR Guardrails operam em tempo real, antes e após a geração de texto, com técnicas como prompt injection detection , output classification e post-hoc moderation . Modelos da Anthropic (Claude) incluem guardrails nativos baseados em Constitutional AI , enquanto OpenAI (GPT) usa Moderation API + system prompts + fine-tuning supervisionado.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
articles.excerpt: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is th…
articles.body: An artist’s concept depicting a Voyager spacecraft. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight this historic milestone with two events. On Tuesday, Nov. 17, NASA invites the world to participate in “Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day” by creating a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset. NASA has created a website that enables smart phones and tablets to flash “VGR”, Voyager’s call sign, in morse code.

articles.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
articles.excerpt: The lopsided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune could be the product of extreme conditions inside the planets, increasing the electrical conductivity that enhances the dynamo effect.
articles.body: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down.
